I work in … / I’m a student. / I’m retired.

questions.support: I’d like to use English when I …

pages.title: Ana and Kim’s favourite trips
pages.subtitle: Read the conversation together, then swap roles.
pages.objective: Use a short conversational model to notice reactions, follow-up questions and a local day out.
pages.source: Original s3 · What was your best trip?

lines.en: Ana, what was your best trip?
lines.pt: Ana, qual foi a sua melhor viagem?

lines.en: A weekend in Ilhabela with my brother, Leo. The best part was the boat trip.
lines.pt: Um fim de semana em Ilhabela com o meu irmão, o Leo. A melhor parte foi o passeio de barco.
Que legal! Deu alguma coisa errada?

lines.en: Yes! It rained all day on Sunday, so we played cards at the hotel. What about you?
lines.pt: Sim! Choveu o dia todo no domingo, então jogamos cartas no hotel. E você?

lines.en: My best day out was a Sunday in Bom Retiro, in São Paulo. It felt like home!
lines.pt: Meu melhor passeio foi um domingo no Bom Retiro, em São Paulo. Eu me senti em casa!

lines.en: I love that! Where would you like to go next?
lines.pt: Adorei! Aonde você gostaria de ir agora?

lines.en: I’d love to go to Salvador. The food looks amazing!
lines.pt: Eu adoraria ir para Salvador. A comida parece incrível!

pages.followup: How does Ana react to Kim’s story? Find her words.

pages.title: Comprehension questions
pages.subtitle: Answer the questions about the conversation.
pages.objective: Understand details and notice a natural reaction.

questions.q: What was the best part of Ana’s trip?
Why did Ana play cards at the hotel?
questions.answer: It rained all day on Sunday.

questions.q: How does Ana react to Kim’s story?

pages.title: Beach or mountains?
pages.subtitle: Choose a place, explain why, and ask your teacher.
pages.objective: Give a preference and reason; invite the other person’s view.
pages.source: Original s41 · The beach or the mountains?
pages.followup: What do you like doing there?

pages.title: Big city or small town?
pages.subtitle: Compare the two and share a place you know.
pages.objective: Extend a preference with a simple comparison and a concrete example.
pages.source: Original s42 · A big city or a small town?
pages.followup: Which city or town would you recommend?
support: … is more relaxing / more exciting than …

pages.title: Plane or bus?
pages.subtitle: Explain your choice for a trip you would like to take.
pages.objective: Connect a choice of transport with a destination and a practical reason.
pages.source: Original s43 · By plane or by bus?
pages.followup: Where would you go, and how long would you stay?

pages.title: Your travel story
pages.subtitle: Tell a story, then keep the conversation going.
pages.objective: Sustain a personal narrative with less support and initiate follow-up questions.
pages.source: Original s5 · Let’s talk + original s3 Your turn
pages.prompt: Think of a trip or a day out you remember well.
steps: Where did you go, and who did you go with?
Did anything go wrong? What happened?
extension: What would you do differently next time?
Where would you like to go next, and why?
pages.ask: Now ask your teacher about a trip. Ask a follow-up question, too.

pages.title: Make it yours
pages.subtitle: Choose two phrases and finish with your own ideas.
pages.objective: Consolidate useful language and articulate a personally meaningful next step.
starters: I’d love to go to … because …
pages.reflection: What would you like to talk about in your next class?

teacherNotes.principle: 30-minute trial, mainly oral interaction. Read the model live. No answer key for personal responses. Offer a local day out, imagined trip or familiar outing if travel is not available. Use support only when needed; listen before expanding. Do not correct every error.
teacherNotes.story: Allow 60–90 seconds for the first story. Respond naturally, then invite the learner to ask two questions. Optional extensions are conversation choices, not a checklist or assessment.

audio.reason: The three picture-talk labels use approved ElevenLabs recordings. Read the model dialogue live; no recorded dialogue or speech-synthesis fallback.
